meta: In part 4, AI read a whole library. But then it could only continue sentences like a parrot, not answer you. Part 5 explains how the "parrot" becomes a helpful assistant.
prompt: I'm a middle school teacher. Keep answers short, with examples. Use a friendly, informal tone.

muc.title: A parrot that only continues
muc.text: Last time, AI read a whole library. But at that point it's like a parrot: it can only continue sentences, not answer you.

muc.title: You ask one thing, it says another
muc.text: Ask it how to sleep better, and it might continue with a list of other questions, because online, questions often sit next to each other like that.

muc.title: Learning from sample conversations
muc.text: Next, people write lots of sample conversations: if asked this, answer like that. AI copies them, and starts answering the actual question.

muc.title: People give scores
muc.text: Then AI writes a few different answers, and people score which is better. Helpful, polite, honest answers get rewarded. Made-up or dangerous answers lose points.

muc.title: Why AI knows how to say no
muc.text: This is also when AI learns to refuse harmful requests, and learns the polite tone you see every day.

muc.title: Teach AI about you
muc.text: Go to the personalization settings and write three lines: who you are, whether you want long or short answers, and how to talk to you. Give good answers a thumbs up, bad ones a thumbs down, and say why.

muc.title: Ask twice, get two answers?
muc.text: But why does asking the same question twice give two different answers? Part six has the answer.
